# Spotlight on Lineage in the Pacific Northwest: Connecting food production, ports and distribution


October 09, 2026


Share This Article


[Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/spotlight-pacific-northwest-cold-storage&title=Spotlight%20on%20Lineage%20in%20the%20Pacific%20Northwest:%20Connecting%20food%20production,%20ports%20and%20distribution)[LinkedIn](http://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/spotlight-pacific-northwest-cold-storage&title=Spotlight%20on%20Lineage%20in%20the%20Pacific%20Northwest:%20Connecting%20food%20production,%20ports%20and%20distribution&source=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/spotlight-pacific-northwest-cold-storage)[Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/spotlight-pacific-northwest-cold-storage&title=Spotlight%20on%20Lineage%20in%20the%20Pacific%20Northwest:%20Connecting%20food%20production,%20ports%20and%20distribution&hashtags=onelineage)


The[Pacific Northwest](https://www.onelineage.com/pacific-northwest-region) brings several parts of the food supply chain together. It’s a growing region for fruits and vegetables, an important hub for seafood and a gateway to trade with Canada, Asia-Pacific and South America. Food businesses here serve customers across the region while moving products into and out of international markets.


Those opportunities come with complexity. Harvests and catches vary, geography can complicate transportation and shifts in pricing, inventory and tariffs can change a shipping plan overnight. Businesses need options for where they store products, how they prepare them and which routes they take to market.


Lineage supports those needs through 30 facilities across the Pacific Northwest, connecting[cold storage](https://www.onelineage.com/services/cold-storage-warehousing) with[transportation](https://www.onelineage.com/services/global-integrated-solutions) , port access and specialized services. From Eastern Washington’s production areas to the waterfront in Seattle, that network helps customers coordinate more of their food supply chain within one provider.


## Connecting regional production with routes to market


Lineage’s Pacific Northwest footprint includes more than 1.3 million pallet positions and over 9.3 million square feet of temperature-controlled space. Facilities along Puget Sound, in Eastern Washington and near the Canadian border put that capacity close to different sources of supply and demand.


Access to major roadways, like the I-5, I-90 and I-84 connects the network to large population centers across the region, while links to the ports of Seattle, Tacoma and Bellingham support international shipments. For our customers, those connections offer flexibility to plan around production needs, shipping schedules and the markets they serve.


## Bringing seafood and international trade through Seattle-Tacoma


In Seattle-Tacoma, Lineage operates five[port-centric facilities](https://www.onelineage.com/services/port-centric-warehousing) with more than 120,000 pallet positions. These locations support seafood, proteins, consumer packaged goods, retail and[foodservice](https://www.onelineage.com/services/foodservice-solutions) customers in a major population and trade center.


The Seattle-Tacoma network offers deep-water terminal access and capabilities like direct vessel offload and direct container loading for exports. Those services connect waterfront operations with the storage and handling that products need before their next move.


On-site processing, temperature reduction and USDA and FDA inspections[help customers prepare products](https://www.onelineage.com/services/food-processing-solutions) for onward shipment. Transloading and[rail capabilities](https://www.onelineage.com/services/temperature-controlled-rail) provide even more transportation options. Together, these services help businesses coordinate the work between arrival at the port and departure for their next destination.


## Supporting food production in Greater Portland


Greater Portland’s food businesses handle a broad mix of products, from frozen[fruits and vegetables](https://www.onelineage.com/services/fresh-and-perishable-solutions) to fish, dairy and consumer packaged goods. Lineage’s four locations in the area support that mix with more than 80,000 pallet positions and over 19 million cubic feet of space.


Capabilities include temperature reduction, production support, case picking and[blast freezing services](https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/blast-freezing-services-spotlight) at our[Woodland facility](https://www.onelineage.com/facilities/woodland) . These services address different points in a product’s journey, whether it needs freezing after production or picking to fulfill a customer order.


Having production support close to storage and transportation helps customers plan those steps together. It also gives food businesses a regional base for preparing inventory and moving it toward the markets they serve.


## Matching Eastern Washington’s agricultural scale


In Eastern Washington, the focus turns to the region’s potato, fruit and vegetable production. Lineage has ten locations here, with more than 640,000 pallet positions and over 144 million cubic feet of space.


That capacity supports a part of the food supply chain where the[volume and timing of harvests shape storage and shipping needs](https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/growing-without-pains) . On-site production capabilities connect the work of preparing food with the space needed to hold it.


Highway and rail access, along with[drayage services](https://www.onelineage.com/services/drayage) , support movement beyond the growing region. For producers, the combination helps connect local operations with the broader transportation network needed to reach customers.


## Linking northern Washington with Canada and maritime trade


Farther north, Lineage’s four locations in Whatcom and Skagit counties support seafood, berries, proteins, prepared foods and consumer packaged goods. With more than 170,000 pallet positions, these facilities are positioned to support businesses trading with Canada.


The area’s capabilities include a port-centric facility, direct vessel offload, railcar loading and tramper vessel loading and unloading. USDA and FDA inspections, on-site processing tenants and a quick freezing tunnel support additional product handling needs.


Dry storage, bulk storage and racked storage add flexibility for different inventory requirements. This wide range of services gives customers options for handling products arriving by water, moving across the border or awaiting distribution.


## Keeping storage, specialized services and transportation connected


Across the Pacific Northwest, a shipment may need several services before it is ready for its next destination. Lineage’s wide range of regional capabilities help customers coordinate that work alongside cold storage.


Transportation services carry those connections beyond the facility. Drayage,[customs brokerage](https://www.onelineage.com/services/customs-brokerage) ,[less-than-truckload shipping](https://www.onelineage.com/services/less-than-truckload-shipping) and[over-the-road transportation](https://www.onelineage.com/services/managed-transportation) support domestic and international movements. Cross-border less-than-truckload and full truckload services support customers moving products between markets.


The value is in how those services work together. A producer planning around a harvest, a seafood business receiving a vessel and an importer arranging cross-border transportation each have different needs. Lineage’s[Pacific Northwest network](https://www.onelineage.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/Lineage%20PNW%20Regional%20One%20Sheeter.pdf) gives them access to regional capacity and capabilities within a broader supply chain.


From the growing areas inland to the ports along the coast, Lineage connects where food comes from with where it needs to go.
